signup_form.note: Hosted landing page from the "College" template; double opt-in on by default; the confirmation email reached Gmail's main inbox

import_export.exported_fields: first name, email, created date, status, tags, city/state/country, referrer, UTM fields and cancelled date
import_export.note: export arrives as an emailed download link valid for 5 days

welcome_sequence.note: Not on the Free plan: Kit's help page lists email sequences as a paid-plan (Creator and up) feature. During the trial the sequence editor did open

problems: The test issue landed in Gmail's spam folder. It was sent from a Gmail address through Kit's servers ("via n.convertkit.com"). The double opt-in confirmation email from the same address reached the main inbox.
To send, you have to press "Continue" at the bottom right of the publish screen, which was easy to miss.
Right after adding a subscriber by hand, the list still showed 0 until the page was refreshed.
Export is tucked under a "…" menu in a pop-up at the bottom of the screen.
notes: There was no plan choice at sign-up: a 14-day trial of paid features started automatically. Kit filled in a US mailing address in the email footer, so no home address was needed. Emails carry a "Built with Kit" badge.
tester_comment: It was easier than I expected, but the test email going to spam worried me.

screenshots.caption: Right after sign-up: no plan choice, a 14-day trial started automatically (bottom left).
Writing the first email starts with a template choice. We picked "Text only".
The test issue in Kit's editor. Kit filled in a US mailing address in the footer and adds a "Built with Kit" badge.
Send settings. The From address was our Gmail address. To actually send, you press "Continue" at the bottom right (not shown), which was easy to miss.
Where it landed: Gmail's spam folder, "via n.convertkit.com".
Sign-up form test: a landing page from the "College" template after subscribing. Double opt-in is on by default.
CSV import: Kit matched both columns to the right fields automatically.
Export isn't a direct download: Kit emails a link that expires after 5 days.
The sequence editor opened during the trial. Kit's help page lists email sequences as a paid-plan feature.
